correctness.rationale: PASS — Three independent Gaussian vertices admit independent edge sum and difference U,V with covariances 6Σ and 2Σ. Their radial-exponential ratios reduce the obtuse-angle probability to the stated single angular integral. Symmetrizing independent arcsine-distributed cos² angles gives A(R)=1/4−(9/4)E[(q(S)−q(T))²/(3q(S)²+10q(S)q(T)+3q(T)²)]. Since q_R=1+(R−1)s, the integrand is strictly increasing with R>1 for s≠t by a positive normalized variance derivative, proving all-R strict decrease; at R=1 it vanishes. The arcsine moment variance 1/8 yields the 9/256 quadratic loss. The large-R endpoint layer is controlled separately, giving sqrt(3)/π·log(R)/R+O(R^-1), with nondegenerate finite R and limiting R→∞ distinguished. A separate SciPy adaptive quadrature gives A(1)=0.25, A(2)=0.233776306839877, A(16)=0.0951255750851252, A(10000)=0.0005131827413711 and normalized tail 0.5571811; finite quadrature is a check, not an infinite proof.
